newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine ex-minister stands by Menem graft slur.
newsitem.headline: Argentine ex-minister stands by Menem graft slur.

text.p: A former Argentine interior minister refused before a federal judge on Monday to retract comments accusing President Carlos Menem of having "no credibility" to combat corruption.

"I ratify what I said and how I said it, which was that Menem is not credible, and I will continue to say it," Gustavo Beliz told reporters after a mandatory conciliation meeting with Menem's lawyers at a federal courthouse.

Gustavo Beliz was Menem's youthful interior minister from 1992-93 but left the Peronist government calling it a "viper's nest" of corruption. He now leads his own New Leadership party which fared badly in Buenos Aires elections this year.
Once Menem's protege and speechwriter, Beliz is being sued for comments he made after the Peronist chief announced an anti-graft crusade to clean up the public sector.
The suit quotes Beliz saying "society does not believe the president when he says he will fight against the mafia because a large part of the public sees him almost as the boss..."
Beliz denied he actually called Menem a mafia boss, but said he stood by his comments that Menem "doesn't even believe it himself when he says he is fighting the mafia."
Menem's attorney Ricardo Klass said "the case against the ex-minister will go ahead because there was no retraction."

Another former minister, Menem's highly successful economy chief Domingo Cavallo whom he sacked in July, is being sued by one minister and threatened with legal action by another for accusing them of covering up official corruption.
